candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: transitTime
candidates.comment: A transit time relation between shipping conditions or delivery time and the typical delay between dispatch and customer receipt. Also called delivery time, shipping duration, lead time. Examples: "ShippingConditions transitTime 'PT3D'", "ShippingDeliveryTime transitTime '2-5 business days'", "ShippingConditions transitTime 'PT72H'".

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: boardingPolicy
candidates.comment: A type of boarding policy used by an airline or for a flight. Also called: boarding procedure, airline boarding rules. Examples: "Airline 'United' boardingPolicy 'BoardingPolicyType.ZoneBoarding'", "Flight 'Flight 789' boardingPolicy 'Group-based boarding'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: interactivityType
candidates.comment: A learning mode relation between a creative work and the predominant way it supports learning. Also called learning style, engagement mode, pedagogical approach. Examples: A textbook has an interactivityType of 'expositive'. An online quiz has an interactivityType of 'active'. A workshop has an interactivityType of 'mixed'.

candidates.label: interactionStatistic
candidates.comment: An interaction metric relation between a creative work, organization, or person, and a counter that quantifies user interactions with it. Also called engagement metrics, user activity, interaction data, usage statistics. Examples: A blog post has an interactionStatistic of a 'LikeAction' counter. An organization has an interactionStatistic of a 'CommentAction' counter. A person has an interactionStatistic of a 'ShareAction' counter.

candidates.label: interactionCount
candidates.comment: A deprecated property indicating the number of user interactions with an item. Also called user interactions, engagement count, activity count. Examples: (No active examples for deprecated properties).

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: interactionType
candidates.comment: A classification relation between an interaction counter and the specific type of action it represents. Also called type of engagement, action category, interaction kind. Examples: An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'LikeAction'. An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'CommentAction'. An interaction counter has an interactionType of 'ShareAction'.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: actionableFeedbackPolicy
candidates.comment: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy. Examples: "A news organization's actionable feedback policy is its 'Corrections and Feedback' page.", "The company's actionable feedback policy outlines how customers can submit suggestions."

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: agent

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: directors
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, episode, movie, or video game and the persons who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmakers, showrunners. Examples: "Movie" directors "Joel Coen, Ethan Coen", "TV Episode" directors "Various Directors", "Video Game" directors "Hideo Kojima, Yoji Shinkawa". Distinct from director, which is a singular property for a single director.

candidates.label: director
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, creative work season, episode, event, movie, or video game and a person who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmaker, showrunner. Examples: "Movie" director "Steven Spielberg", "TV Episode" director "Ava DuVernay", "Video Game" director "Hideo Kojima". Distinct from directors, which is a plural property for multiple directors.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".
